newsitem.title: JAPAN: Impact of Dow fall on Japan's economy limited -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Impact of Dow fall on Japan's economy limited -- EPA.

text.p: The fall in Wall Street stocks on Friday will have little impact on the Japanese economy, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Tuesday.
He said although Friday's fall had been quite large, the drop differed from "Black Monday" in 1987 as the Dow's current level is still quite high despite the losses.
"The influence of the fall will not be that large," he said.
Aso added that the U.S. economy is still healthy and this would be good for imports from Japan.

He said although there was some concern about the Japanese economy, such as stagnant private consumption, there were also positive factors working in the economy such as industrial output and capital spending.

He said he was asked these questions on the economy by the government's Management and Coordination Agency chief Kabun Muto. When asked by Muto if he had any worries about the Japanese economy, Aso said he told Muto: "It is not as if there are no worries. We are watching the economy closely. It is not like we have to be on full alert."
